newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares sag but close above 4,100 SMI points.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares sag but close above 4,100 SMI points.

text.p: 1530 GMT - Swiss shares ended one percent lower on the back of Wall Street's slump on Thursday but the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) managed to close above 4,100 points after temporarily falling below that level.

Dealers said a correction had been expected. "The reaction is normal after the market has long been overbought," one trader said, adding that prospects for further gains remained good. "I have the feeling there won't be any U.S. interest rate hike anytime soon", he said. Another trader said the possibility of higher U.S. interest rates may continue to weigh on the market.
* SMI fell 35.5 points, or 0.85 percent, to 4,125.5.
On Thursday, the SMI closed at a record 4,161.0 points. Today's low was at 4,082.7.
* All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended down 20.62 points, or 0.78 percent, to 2,639.47

* The highflyers of the past few days were under heavy pressure. Roche certificates, which had hit an all-time high of 12,500 francs on Wednesday, slumped 200 francs, or 1.67 percent, to 11,780. The mid-week jump had been triggered by rumours that Roche may plan a merger or a divestment.
* Thursday's prominent winner UBS also gave up ground. The bearer shares lost nine francs to 1,180.
* Swissair, Surveillance, Novartis, Sulzer, SMH registered shares, Alusuisse and insurers Zirich and Swiss Re also fell more than one percent each.

* Insurer Winterthur, chemical firm Clariant, and temporary employment company Adecco posted solid gains. Traders said Winterthur was sought by a bank, adding 15 francs to 833. Clariant rose 39 francs, or 5.97 percent, to 692. Adecco gained 11 francs to 406 on high volume, profiting from hopes for job market liberalisation in Germany and Italy, one dealer said.
CS Holding posted a gain of 0.25 francs to 141.25 after being in negative terrain most of the day.
* On the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex), trade calmed down after Thursday's hectic session, dealers said.
Total volume in options was 107,284 after 241,888 contracts on Thursday. Demand was higher for SMI futures, where volume stood at 6,967 contracts.
Implicit volatilities were generally stable. An increase in volatilities could be seen in options on Winterthur, CS Group and SMH, dealers said.
